compounding_issues: No .gitignore was ever created: node_modules/ and dist/ are committed in every session, making session 1 alone ~968K insertions across 5153 files and bloating every subsequent diff (session 5 still carries dist/ churn)
Session 1's hardcoded inline HTML (buildPageHTML/buildIndexHTML) was a throwaway design that session 2 replaced wholesale with the Handlebars engine — dead-end code and wasted effort
Session 4's plugin config loader probes process.cwd()/__dirname with a runtime require() of a .ts config — fragile, best-effort surface with no test coverage
BuildContext and SSGConfig leak `any` across the plugin seam, and session 5's caching threads through plugins via structural casts ((page as any)._fromCache), eroding type safety

DevServerPlugin bypasses the lifecycle contract it defines — it exposes start()/setEngine()/getInstance() instead of implementing behavior in onStart/afterBuild, so the dev server is not driven through the plugin pipeline
Convention adherence stayed flat at ~0.46 across all five sessions (naming/PascalCase violations plus an unused @types/handlebars deprecated stub dependency)
key_decisions: Session 1 fixed the foundation: marked + gray-matter + yargs + strict TypeScript + jest, with a build-only CLI
Session 2 introduced a Handlebars TemplateEngine (default layouts, per-page templates, partials) that replaced the hardcoded HTML layer and rewrote ssg.ts
Session 3 added a chokidar + WebSocket live-reload dev server behind `npx ssg serve` without breaking the existing build or its tests
Session 4 extracted a hook-based plugin system (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with built-in Markdown/Template/DevServer plugins and ssg.config.ts, collapsing serve.ts to a thin wrapper
Session 5 layered a CacheManager content-hash manifest with --incremental/--clean flags and build stats onto the plugin pipeline rather than bypassing it
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily and monotonically. Session 1 produced a functional but monolithic SSG with hardcoded string HTML; session 2 was the largest quality jump, replacing that dead-end markup with a proper Handlebars engine (layouts/partials) while tripling test coverage (137→323 lines). Session 3 integrated a live-reload dev server cleanly and earned the best commit review (architectural fit 0.85, no debt). Session 4 was a behavior-preserving architectural refactor — 495 insertions / 315 deletions, no tests broken — that matured the codebase into a modular plugin pipeline, though it introduced `any` leaks at the seam. Session 5 added incremental caching with the largest single test file (376 lines). Test lines grew from 137 to ~961 across the arc and every session honored the don't-break-existing-behavior constraint, so the code moved from a monolithic generator to a modular, extensible, cache-aware one — with repo hygiene (committed node_modules/dist) as the one metric that never improved.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, quality-ascending 5-session arc — greenfield monolith → template engine → dev server → plugin architecture → incremental caching — marred only by persistent repo-hygiene debt (committed node_modules/dist) and a throwaway session-1 HTML layer.
